implementation_notes: The query object is the expression tree the C# compiler emits for a lambda: Expression<Func<T,bool>> captures the lambda as data, and IQueryable<T> composes trees through Where/Select/OrderBy/Join extension methods that return a new query for each clause while a provider (EF Core, LINQ to SQL) translates the tree to SQL. What replaces the classic query-builder class is the language itself plus the provider's visitor; the hand-built builder stays justified only when trees must be composed dynamically through Expression.Call/Lambda or exposed to non-LINQ consumers.
pitfalls: Only expression lambdas become trees: a statement-bodied lambda compiles to a delegate and silently switches evaluation to memory.
Provider translation is partial - constructs that cannot be translated throw at runtime, so assert the generated SQL in tests instead of assuming.
Deferred execution: an IQueryable captured with its DbContext cannot outlive that context, and enumerating it twice executes it twice.
